title: Points that land on the median
brief:
You are counting a run for the shift rule (six or more consecutive points on one side of the median). As you count along, you reach a point whose value is **exactly equal to the median**.

How should you treat it?

task.stem: How do you treat a point that lands exactly on the median when counting a shift?

options.label: Count it as above the median.
Count it as below the median.
Skip it — points on the median don't count toward the run, and they don't reset it.
Start the count over from that point.

debrief.correct: Correct. A point sitting **exactly on the median** is neither above nor below, so you **skip it** — it does not add to the run, and it does not break or reset it. You simply carry on counting the points either side. Treating on-median points as above or below (or restarting the count) is a common way people miscount a shift.
debrief.wrong: A point exactly on the median is neither above nor below it, so it can't count toward a run on either side. The convention is to **skip it** — it doesn't add to the run and doesn't reset it; you keep counting the points that are clearly above or below. This is why the median (not the mean) is used and why 'points on the line' need a rule of their own.
debrief.rule_cited: Counting runs and shifts — points on the median are excluded — Provost & Murray (2nd ed.), IHI QI 104.
